description: vLLM serving Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 on desg0 (single engine, scraped at desg0:8000, job "vllm"). Engine limits it is read against (hosts/desg0/vllm_qwen3_container.nix): --max-num-seqs 32, --max-model-len 262144, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6, --kv-cache-dtype fp8. Traffic is bursty agent traffic, so request-level rates and histogram quantiles use fixed 30m windows; only the per-token histogram (inter-token latency, millions of samples) uses 5m. Means are rate(_sum)/rate(_count), which is restart-safe. Note: prefix caching is OFF for this hybrid qwen3_5 architecture (vllm:cache_config_info{enable_prefix_caching="False"}), so all prefix-cache / cached-token series stay at 0 -- they live in the collapsed "Caching" row. vllm:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total is also always 0 on this build, so no MFU panel.
title: vllm

panels.description: Finished requests per hour (all finished reasons), 30m smoothed.
panels.title: Requests / h

panels.description: Output (generation) tokens per second across all streams, 30m smoothed. The headline serving throughput.
panels.title: Generation tok/s

panels.description: Requests currently in model execution batches. Hard cap is --max-num-seqs 32; sitting at 32 with a non-empty queue means the engine is saturated.
panels.title: Running requests (max 32)

panels.description: Requests queued for scheduling. Anything sustained above 0 means clients are paying queue time; the reason breakdown is in the Scheduler row.
panels.title: Waiting requests

panels.description: KV cache utilization (1 = full). The cache is sized by --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 with fp8 KV; long agent contexts (up to 262144 tokens) eat it fast. Sustained ~1 causes queueing and preemptions.
panels.title: KV cache usage

panels.description: p95 time to first token over the last 30m. Dominated by prefill of long agent prompts plus queue time; this is what makes an agent feel slow to start.
panels.title: TTFT p95

panels.description: Time to first token: how long a client waits before the stream starts. = queue time + prefill. Histogram buckets top out at 2560s, so quantiles are trustworthy across the whole range.
panels.title: Time to first token

panels.description: Inter-token latency: the gap between consecutive tokens of one stream, i.e. perceived typing speed (1 / ITL = tokens/s per client). Uses a 5m window because this histogram gets one sample per generated token. Rises with batch size and with KV pressure.
panels.title: Inter-token latency

panels.description: End-to-end request latency (arrival to last token). For long agent generations this is mostly decode time, so it tracks output length rather than engine health -- compare with the phase breakdown to the right.
panels.title: End-to-end request latency

panels.description: Mean seconds a request spends in each phase, 30m window. queue = waiting to be scheduled (should stay near 0), prefill = processing the prompt, decode = generating. Queue growing while decode is flat = admission pressure; prefill growing = prompts getting longer or KV thrash.
panels.title: Mean time per request phase

panels.description: Prompt (prefill) vs generation (decode) tokens per second, 30m smoothed. Prompt spikes mark new/reloaded agent conversations; with prefix caching off every turn re-prefills its whole history.
panels.title: Token rate

panels.description: Finished requests per hour by reason. stop = natural end, length = hit max_tokens (truncated answer), abort = client disconnected, error = engine failure, repetition = stopped by the repetition detector. Anything but stop/length deserves a log check: journalctl -u podman-vllm-qwen3 on desg0.
panels.title: Requests / h by finished reason

panels.description: HTTP responses per hour by handler and status class. 4xx on /v1/chat/completions is the usual symptom of a client sending something the server rejects (e.g. tool_choice without --enable-auto-tool-choice, or a prompt over --max-model-len); 5xx means the engine broke. These requests never reach vllm:request_success_total, so this is the only place they show up.
panels.title: HTTP responses / h by handler & status

panels.description: Tokens processed per engine step (batch efficiency). A step is either a prefill chunk (thousands of tokens) or a decode step (one token per running sequence), so the mean sits just above the number of running requests when idle-ish and jumps during prefills. Low mean with a non-empty queue = the engine is spending its steps on tiny batches.
panels.title: Tokens per engine step

panels.description: Preemptions in the last 24h. A preemption evicts a running request's KV cache to make room for others and re-runs it from scratch -- the clearest sign the KV cache is too small for the offered load (lower --max-num-seqs or raise --gpu-memory-utilization).
panels.title: Preemptions (24h)

panels.description: 1 while the engine is awake. 0 means it went to sleep (weights offloaded or discarded), so the next request pays a wake-up penalty. Nothing in this deployment triggers sleep, so a 0 here is unexpected.
panels.title: Engine awake

panels.description: p95 time requests spent in the WAITING phase over the last 30m. Non-trivial values mean requests are being admitted late, not served slowly.
panels.title: Queue time p95

panels.description: Rejected/failed HTTP requests per hour (4xx + 5xx, all handlers), 30m smoothed. Any sustained value means a client is misconfigured or the engine is erroring; break it down in the HTTP panel above.
panels.title: HTTP 4xx+5xx / h

panels.description: Output tokens per second as a single client experiences it (1 / mean inter-token latency). Independent of how many requests are in flight, unlike the aggregate generation tok/s.
panels.title: Per-stream tok/s

panels.description: Time since the vLLM API server process started. A reset means the container restarted (OOM, rebuild, model reload) and every cumulative counter above restarted with it.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: KV cache utilization over time. Sawtooth = normal scheduling; a plateau near 1 together with waiting requests or preemptions means the cache is the binding constraint. The GPU is shared with llama.cpp and minimax-music3, so the ceiling cannot simply be raised.
panels.title: KV cache usage

panels.description: Scheduler occupancy: running requests (capped at --max-num-seqs 32) against the queue split by reason. capacity = no scheduling room left (KV cache or seq slots), deferred = held back by transient constraints (LoRA budget, KV transfer, blocked status).
panels.title: Running vs waiting requests

panels.description: Prompt tokens per request. Explains prefill cost and TTFT. Caveat: the histogram's largest finite bucket is 50000 tokens, so quantiles saturate there even though --max-model-len is 262144 -- use the mean and the "> 50k share" series to see genuinely huge agent contexts.
panels.title: Prompt tokens per request

panels.description: Generation tokens per request versus the max_tokens clients asked for. When the p95 of generated tokens meets the requested max_tokens, answers are being truncated -- cross-check finished_reason=length.
panels.title: Generation tokens per request

panels.description: Tool-call parser invocations per hour, split by outcome. Streaming increments once per delta, non-streaming once per choice, so treat this as a relative signal: outcome=tool_call vs no_tool_call shows how much of the traffic is agentic. Requires --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder (set in hosts/desg0/vllm_qwen3_container.nix); if this row is empty, agents are not reaching the tool path.
panels.title: Tool-call parser invocations / h

panels.description: Requests per hour by API handler (from the ASGI middleware, so it also counts requests that never reached the engine). /v1/chat/completions is agent traffic; /v1/models is a client discovering the model list at startup (pi does this on every launch).
panels.title: API requests / h by handler

panels.description: Prefix-cache hit ratio (cached query tokens / queried tokens) over 30m. Expected to be empty here: vLLM disables prefix caching for the qwen3_5 hybrid GatedDeltaNet architecture (vllm:cache_config_info{enable_prefix_caching="False"}), so every conversation turn re-prefills its full history. Kept so the loss is visible if a future vLLM release enables it.
panels.title: Prefix cache hit ratio

panels.description: Prompt tokens per second by KV source: local_compute = fresh prefill, local_cache_hit = served from the local prefix cache, external_kv_transfer = from an external KV store. With prefix caching off, everything is local_compute.
panels.title: Prompt tokens by source

panels.description: Scrape health of desg0:8000. 0/no data means the container is down, restarting (model load takes minutes) or the firewall/port changed -- check `systemctl status podman-vllm-qwen3` on desg0.
panels.title: Target up

panels.description: Resident memory of the API server process (host RAM, not GPU memory; the engine core runs in a separate process that does not export process_* metrics). Watch for a slow climb -- the container has no memory limit and shares desg0 with llama.cpp and minimax-music3.
panels.title: API server memory

panels.description: CPU cores burned by the API server process (tokenization, JSON, SSE streaming, tool-call parsing). Approaching 1.0 means the Python front-end -- not the GPU -- is the bottleneck.
panels.title: API server CPU
